title: Shopping & money
goal: Ask prices, point out 'this one' and 'that one', bargain politely and buy clothes in the right size.
intro: Gujarat is a trading culture, and shopping — from Ahmedabad's Law Garden night market to the cloth shops of Surat — comes with friendly bargaining. The key question is **આ કેટલાનું છે?** 'How much is this?'. You'll also learn Gujarati's three-way set of demonstratives: **આ** 'this', **એ / તે** 'that', and **પેલું** 'that one over there'.

vocab.note: m pl · છુટ્ટા છે? 'do you have change?'
થોડા ઓછા કરો 'knock a bit off'

phrases.en: Come on, knock a bit off.
Show me that blue sari over there.
Do you have this in another colour?

grammar.title: This, that and that-over-there
grammar.body:
Gujarati has three demonstratives:

**આ** *ā* — this (near me)
**એ / તે** *e / te* — that (near you, or already mentioned)
**પેલું** *peluṃ* — that one over there (far from both of us; you can point)

As adjectives, **આ, એ, તે do not change**: આ સાડી, આ શર્ટ, આ બૂટ. **પેલું** agrees like any -ઉં adjective: **પેલો** રંગ, **પેલી** સાડી, **પેલું** શર્ટ.

Before postpositions they take oblique forms: **આનું** 'of this', **આમાં** 'in this', **એનું** 'of that', **પેલાનું** 'of that one'. Hence **આનો ભાવ** 'this one's price', **આમાં બીજો રંગ** 'another colour in this'.

examples.en: Show me that kurta over there.

grammar.title: 'The red one': -વાળું and 'which one': કયું
grammar.body:
To say 'the … one', add **વાળું** after an adjective, noun or demonstrative. It agrees with the noun you have in mind: **લાલ વાળી** (sari, f) 'the red one', **મોટા વાળું** (n) 'the big one' (an -ઉં adjective takes its -ā form before વાળું), **આ વાળો** (m) 'this one'.

**કયું** *kayuṃ* 'which' also agrees: **કયો** (m), **કઈ** (f), **કયું** (n), **કયા** (m pl, oblique), **કયાં** (n pl).

Combine them: **કયા વાળું?** 'Which one?' — **પેલા વાળું** 'That one over there.'

examples.en: No, not that, the one over there.

dialogue.title: Bargaining at Law Garden
dialogue.setting: Riya shops for a chaniya choli at the evening market in Ahmedabad's Law Garden.

lines.speaker: Seller
lines.en: Come, ben, what are you looking for?

lines.speaker: Riya
lines.native: નવરાત્રિ માટે ચણિયાચોળી. પેલી લાલ વાળી કેટલાની છે?
lines.roman: navrātri māṭe chaṇiyāchoḷī. pelī lāl vāḷī keṭlānī chhe?
lines.en: A chaniya choli for Navratri. How much is that red one?

lines.speaker: Seller
lines.native: એ તો બહુ સરસ છે. પચ્ચીસસો.
lines.roman: e to bahu saras chhe. pachchīsso.
lines.en: That one's very nice. Twenty-five hundred.

lines.speaker: Riya
lines.native: અરે! બહુ મોંઘી છે. પંદરસોમાં આપો.
lines.roman: are! bahu moṃghī chhe. pandarsomāṃ āpo.
lines.en: Oh! That's very expensive. Give it for fifteen hundred.

lines.speaker: Seller
lines.native: ના બેન, પંદરસોમાં ના પોસાય. બે હજાર છેલ્લો ભાવ.
lines.roman: nā ben, pandarsomāṃ nā posāy. be hajār chhello bhāv.
lines.en: No ben, fifteen hundred isn't possible. Two thousand is the final price.

lines.speaker: Riya
lines.en: Seventeen hundred. That's it, not more than that.

lines.speaker: Seller
lines.en: All right, for you, eighteen hundred. Final.

lines.speaker: Riya
lines.en: OK. Shall I pay by UPI?

lines.speaker: Seller
lines.en: Yes, that's fine. Here's the code.

culture: Bargaining (**ભાવતાલ** *bhāvtāl*) is expected in street markets and small shops but not in malls or fixed-price stores. Keep it light and friendly; a smile and **ભાઈ, થોડા ઓછા કરો ને** goes a long way. Hundreds are counted in Gujarati as '15 hundred' (પંદરસો) or '18 hundred' (અઢારસો) rather than 'one thousand five hundred'. Digital payment by UPI (scanning a QR code) is everywhere, even at vegetable carts.

tip.title: How much is it?
tip.body:
- **આ કેટલાનું છે?** (lit. 'this is of how much?') is the everyday way to ask a price. It agrees with the thing: ચોપડી **કેટલાની** છે?
- Or ask the rate: **ભાવ શું છે?** — કેરી**નો** ભાવ 'the price of mangoes'.
- **મોંઘું / સસ્તું** agree too: મોંઘો (m), મોંઘી (f), મોંઘું (n), મોંઘાં (n pl).
tip.pattern: આ કેટલાનું છે? · X-નો ભાવ શું છે?

sentences.native: આ થેલી સસ્તી છે, ફક્ત સો રૂપિયા.
sentences.roman: ā thelī sastī chhe, fakt so rūpiyā.
sentences.en: This bag is cheap, only a hundred rupees.
I want to buy a new watch.

tip.title: આ, એ and પેલું
tip.body:
- **આ** 'this' (near me), **એ** 'that' (near you, or already mentioned), **પેલું** 'that one over there'.
- આ and એ never change: આ સાડી, આ શર્ટ. **પેલું** agrees: **પેલો** રંગ, **પેલી** સાડી, **પેલું** શર્ટ.
- Before -નું, -માં they become **આ-, એ-, પેલા-**: **આનો** ભાવ, **પેલાનું** માપ.

sentences.en: Show me that shirt over there.
That sari over there is very beautiful.
Bhai, could you show me that colour over there?
What's the price of that one over there?
Clothes are cheap in this shop.

tip.title: 'The red one' and 'which one'
tip.body:
- Add **વાળું** to say 'the … one'. It agrees with the thing you mean: (sari) **લાલ વાળી**, (shirt) **લીલા વાળું**.
- **કયું** 'which' agrees too: **કયો** (m), **કઈ** (f), **કયું** (n), **કયા** (m pl).
- **આવું** 'like this' and **બીજો** 'another' agree the same way: **આવી** સાડી, **બીજા** બૂટ.

sentences.en: A sari? Show me the red one.

sentences.native: આ સાડી નહીં, પેલા વાળી બતાવો.
sentences.roman: ā sāḍī nahīṃ, pelā vāḷī batāvo.
sentences.en: Not this sari, show me the one over there.
The shirt? Give me the green one.
Do you have sandals like these in another colour?

sentences.native: મારી માસી પાસે આવી સાડી છે.
sentences.roman: mārī māsī pāse āvī sāḍī chhe.
sentences.en: My aunt has a sari like this.
I want a different pair of shoes.

sentences.native: હું પહેલાં બીજી દુકાનમાં જોઈ લઉં.
sentences.roman: huṃ pahelāṃ bījī dukānmāṃ joī lauṃ.
sentences.en: Let me have a look in another shop first.

tip.title: Bargaining politely
tip.body:
- Bargaining is normal in markets, but not in malls or **ફિક્સ** (fixed-price) shops.
- **થોડા ઓછા કરો** 'knock a bit off' — **ને** at the end makes it a friendly nudge. ઓછા agrees with રૂપિયા.
- **છેલ્લું** 'last, final' agrees: **છેલ્લો** ભાવ (m), **છેલ્લી** સાડી (f).
tip.pattern: થોડા ઓછા કરો ને · છેલ્લો ભાવ?

sentences.en: Come on, knock ten rupees off.

sentences.native: હું રોજનો ગ્રાહક છું, થોડા ઓછા કરો.
sentences.roman: huṃ rojno grāhak chhuṃ, thoḍā ochhā karo.
sentences.en: I'm a regular customer, knock a bit off.
Do you have this shirt in a smaller size?

sentences.native: આ માપ નાનું છે, મોટું આપો.
sentences.roman: ā māp nānuṃ chhe, moṭuṃ āpo.
sentences.en: This size is too small, give me a bigger one.

sentences.native: ના બેન, અહીં ભાવ ફિક્સ છે.
sentences.roman: nā ben, ahīṃ bhāv fiks chhe.
sentences.en: No, madam, prices are fixed here.

sentences.native: અમે ફક્ત ફિક્સ ભાવમાં વેચીએ છીએ.
sentences.roman: ame fakt fiks bhāvmāṃ vechīe chhīe.
sentences.en: We only sell at fixed prices.

tip.title: Paying: આપું? and ચાલશે?
tip.body:
- **આપું?** 'shall I give/pay?' — the -ઉં form offers or suggests: યુપીઆઇથી આપું?
- **ચાલશે?** 'will it do?': કાર્ડ ચાલશે? → **હા, ચાલશે** or **ના, ફક્ત રોકડા**.
- **હું આ લઈશ** 'I'll take this'; with અમે: **લઈશું**. (More on the future in Unit 17.)

sentences.en: Do you have change for a hundred rupees?
